components.name: OpenVPN tls-crypt-v2 static key (HMAC-SHA256 + AES-256 control-channel wrap)
components.bom-ref: pqs:finding:openvpn-install.sh:3201:OpenVPN tls-crypt-v2 static key (HMAC-SHA256 + AES-256 control-channel wrap)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here (menu option). OpenVPN data-channel CBC is HMAC-authenticated via `auth $HMAC_ALG` (encrypt-then-MAC at the OpenVPN layer), which softens the generic unauthenticated-CBC rating, but CBC+HMAC remains a legacy composition with padding-oracle class risk; the AEAD defaults are preferred. Symmetric cipher — quantum exposure is Grover-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Menu label and version-gate log strings of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD data-channel option — not a standalone Poly1305 use; the cipher value itself is selected at 2869 and negotiated via `data-ciphers`. Linked to ALG-3d4cff53 so the CBOM has one entry, not two.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Default PKI of this installer: Easy-RSA 3.2.6 generates ECDSA (default prime256v1) CA/server/client certificates; the TLS control channel is authenticated by ECDSA-signed certs. Shor-vulnerable — a CRQC could forge the CA. Changeable here via --cert-type/--cert-curve; no quantum-safe PKI exists in OpenVPN/Easy-RSA today, so migration depends on upstream ML-DSA support.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dual role: prime256v1 is the default ECDSA certificate-key curve AND a default ECDH key-exchange group. Both uses are Shor-vulnerable (signature forgery, key-agreement break). Changeable here via --cert-curve and --tls-groups.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Control-channel key agreement of an OpenVPN server deployed by this script — every client handshake is passively capturable today, so harvest-now-decrypt-later applies directly to VPN control and data channels. No PQ KEX exists in current OpenVPN; best available posture here is TLS 1.3 + x25519-only groups. Changeable via --tls-ciphersuites/--tls-groups.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 ECDH for the control-channel key agreement — Shor-vulnerable like all elliptic-curve DH; harvest-now-decrypt-later. Changeable here via --tls-groups; migration needs OpenVPN support for hybrid groups (e.g. X25519MLKEM768).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Stronger NIST curves offered as alternatives to the prime256v1 default for both ECDSA certs and ECDH groups — larger keys only delay Shor breakage, they do not prevent it. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Primary AEAD data-channel family of the deployed OpenVPN server (default AES-128-GCM). Symmetric — quantum exposure is Grover-only; no Shor break. Changeable here via --cipher. Test-harness sites verify this installer's own output, so they are genuine configuration surface for this product.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-GCM is the DEFAULT data-channel cipher: a 128-bit key leaves only ~64-bit security under Grover, thin margin for a long-lived VPN. Changing the default to AES-256-GCM is a one-line change here. Also covers the AES-128 component of ECDHE suites and the TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 TLS 1.3 suite.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Strongest symmetric option offered; ~128-bit Grover margin — the recommended choice for PQ headroom in current OpenVPN. Changeable here via --cipher/--tls-ciphersuites.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AEAD alternative data-channel cipher for devices without AES-NI; symmetric, Grover-only exposure. Changeable here (menu option 7).
